$comment: The complete client/server boundary surface, and the protocol version that
describes it. Every name here crosses between the React client and the R or
Python server, so adding, renaming, or removing one is a protocol change.
This file exists to make that unavoidable. All three languages assert their
live surface against it: the JS suite scans pkg-js/src, the Python suite
reads shiny's input-handler registry after importing shinyreact, and the R
suite reads the same registry after loading the package. Introduce a new
custom message type or handler name and those tests fail until you add it
here -- next to protocolVersion, where the question 'does this need a
version bump?' is impossible to miss.
Adding a name here is NOT automatically a version bump. Both sides degrade
gracefully for purely additive changes (an older server never sends the new
message; an older client never sends the new input), and the client compares
only major versions, so a minor bump is documentation rather than
enforcement. The bump policy itself is still open -- see issue #232.

customMessages.shinyReactMessage: server -> client, payload {id, data}; consumed by useShinyMessageHandler()
customMessages.shinyreact-deps: server -> client, list of createWebDependency() results; the client renders them and re-runs bindAll

inputHandlers.shinyreact.default: implicit; the JS hook appends it to every untyped input id
inputHandlers.shinyreact.init: per-session bootstrap; installs renderer dep discovery in R, no-op in Python

inputIds..shinyreact_init: sent once per session after Shiny initializes, with the shinyreact.init handler

domIds.shinyreact-config: the JSON script tag carrying protocolVersion and any bookmark restore payload
